title: 2021 Fall AMC 12A Problem 19
statement: Let \(x\) be the least real number greater than \(1\) such that \(\sin(x) = \sin(x^2),\) where the arguments are in degrees. What is \(x\) rounded up to the closest integer?

solutions.text:
Equal sines require \(x^2 = x + 360k\) or \(x^2 = 180 - x + 360k\) for some integer \(k.\)

The family \(x^2 = x + 360k\) first exceeds \(1\) at \(k = 1,\) giving \(x \approx 19.5.\) The family \(x^2 = 180 - x + 360k\) with \(k = 0\) gives \(x^2 + x - 180 = 0,\) so \(x = \dfrac{-1 + \sqrt{721}}{2} \approx 12.93,\) which is smaller.

Rounded up, \(x = 13.\)

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: \(\sin x = \sin x^2\) requires \(x^2 = x + 360k\) or \(x^2 = 180 - x + 360k\) for an integer \(k\)
